cities.base: Old Town, inside or right against the medieval walls, walkable to everything
cities.name: Tallinn

cities.base: Kuressaare, the only real town on the island, next to the castle
cities.name: Saaremaa (Kuressaare)

cities.base: day trip from Tallinn, no overnight
cities.name: Lahemaa National Park

places.name: Patkuli Viewing Platform
places.note: Best skyline shot of the spires and harbour, free and open at all hours, and less packed than Kohtuotsa a few minutes away.

places.name: Seaplane Harbour (Lennusadam)
places.note: A submarine you walk through inside a seaplane hangar, good for kids and adults alike; the ticket is EUR 22 (about $25), open 10:00 to 18:00, closed Mondays, give it two hours.

places.name: Raekoja Plats (Town Hall Square)
places.note: The postcard square, free and open at all hours; the cafes around the edge overcharge, so come for the buildings rather than the coffee, and late in the evening once the tour groups clear out.

places.name: Kadriorg Park and Palace
places.note: The palace is now the Kadriorg Art Museum, about $17, open 10:00 to 18:00 and to 20:00 on Wednesdays, closed Mondays; the park around it is free and far quieter than the old town, and Kumu is a short walk on.

places.name: Olde Hansa
places.note: Medieval theme restaurant, costumed staff and candlelight, food is decent but you're paying for the atmosphere, book ahead

places.name: Rataskaevu 16
places.note: Solid Estonian and European menu without the medieval costumes, better food than most old town options, reserve ahead

places.name: Balti Jaam Market
places.note: Two floor indoor market next to the train station, fresh produce upstairs and food stalls downstairs, more local than anything in old town

places.name: Fat Margaret Tower
places.note: Maritime museum branch inside a defensive tower, EUR 16 (about $18) or EUR 30 combined with Seaplane Harbour; 10:00 to 18:00 from October to April, closed Mondays. Skip it unless maritime history is your thing.

places.name: Telliskivi Creative City
places.note: Converted factory complex with bars, small shops and street art, good on a rainy day since much of it is covered; the complex lists 11:00 to 19:00 on weekdays and 11:00 to 17:00 at weekends.

places.name: Viru Raba (Viru Bog Trail)
places.note: 3.5km boardwalk loop over raised bog with a wooden viewing tower partway round, well maintained and flat, gets busy with tour buses by midday so go early.

places.name: Palmse Manor
places.note: Restored baroque manor house of the Pahlen family, park administration is based here, formal gardens and outbuildings are worth the wander even if you skip the paid interior tour.

places.name: Sagadi Manor
places.note: Smaller and less visited than Palmse, working forest museum on site, good for the forestry history angle rather than grand rooms.

places.name: Kasmu village
places.note: Former captains' village on the coast, wooden houses, boulder-strewn shoreline, called the erratic boulder capital of Estonia for the glacial rocks scattered along the beach.

places.name: Vosu Beach
places.note: Longest sand beach in Lahemaa, pleasant in summer, closed off and windswept most of the year, more a stop for the walk than swimming unless it's July.

places.name: Altja fishing village
places.note: Restored net sheds and swing on the shore, one of the most photographed spots in the park, small enough to see in half an hour.

places.name: Oandu forest nature trail
places.note: Short loop trail through old-growth mixed forest along the Altja river, quiet, no crowds, good option if Viru Bog feels too touristed.

places.name: Kolga Manor
places.note: Manor is in a state of disrepair and mostly closed, only worth a photo stop from the road if you're already passing, not a destination in itself.

places.name: Vihula Manor
places.note: Now a spa hotel and restaurant complex built around the old manor buildings, fine for a coffee stop or lunch, not much to see if you're not a guest.

places.name: Kasmu Maritime Museum
places.note: One room, volunteer run, tells the smuggling and seafaring history of the village, opens irregularly so treat it as a bonus if the door happens to be open.

places.name: Kolga-Aabla area coastal walk
places.note: Quiet stretch of coastline and reed beds around Kolga Bay, good for birdwatching, almost nobody stops here which is either the appeal or the problem depending on what you want.

places.name: Viinistu Art Museum
places.note: Private collection of Estonian art housed in a converted Soviet-era fish factory in a tiny harbour village, incongruous and worth the detour if you have a car and the extra hour.

places.name: Toompea Hill and the old town walls
places.note: The walls and gate towers are the reason Tallinn's old town reads as medieval rather than restored.

places.name: Kuressaare Episcopal Castle
places.note: A moated medieval bishop's castle that also holds the Saaremaa Museum, and the reason to make the crossing; about $15, 11:00 to 18:00, closed Mondays and Tuesdays, two hours.

places.name: Panga Cliff
places.note: A modest limestone cliff by Baltic standards, but the coastline around it is worth the drive.

places.name: Viru Bog Boardwalk
places.note: A flat boardwalk loop through bog pools, easy enough for anyone, and the best reason to leave Tallinn for a day.

places.name: Toompea Hill
places.note: Seat of parliament and old power center, free to wander, gets crowded by midday with tour groups.

places.name: Tallinn Town Wall and Tower Viru Gates
places.note: The Viru Gate towers are free to walk through at any hour; climbing a stretch of the ticketed wall near Hellemann tower gives a sense of scale you miss at street level, but its hours vary, check.

places.name: Lore Bistroo
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026 bistro in the Noblessner shipyard district; order the fish soup (EUR 11.50) and the pike perch (EUR 26, menu checked November 2026). Sunday is 13:00 to 20:00 only, and hours vary, check.

places.name: Mantel ja Korsten
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026 near Kadriorg; the duck is EUR 20 and mains run EUR 14 to 34 (menu checked November 2026). Dinner from 17:00 Tuesday to Friday, from 14:00 at weekends, closed Mondays.

places.name: Tuljak
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026 in Pirita; order the lamb dumplings, beef tartare or Baltic herring. The price is a $50 to $100 a head range (EnPrimeur, September 2026), so $75 is the midpoint; hours vary, check.

places.name: Art Museum of Estonia (Kumu)
places.note: The main building of the Art Museum of Estonia, 4.7 on Google from 6,104 reviews; EUR 16 (about $18), closed Mondays, open to 20:00 on Thursdays, and worth two and a half hours.

places.name: Kiek in de Kök Fortification Museum
places.note: The old town's fortification museum, open 11:00 to 18:00 every day; about $19, free on the first Sunday of each month, and 90 minutes covers it.

places.name: Vabamu Museum of Occupations and Freedom
places.note: The museum to see if you want to understand the occupation years before you walk the old town; about $17, open 10:00 to 18:00 every day, 90 minutes.

places.name: Estonian Open Air Museum
places.note: Old farms spread over a big park at Rocca al Mare; EUR 14 (about $16). In winter (29 September to 22 April) the farms open 10:00 to 17:00 Tuesday to Sunday, part of the exposition is shut, and the park runs to 19:00.

places.name: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral
places.note: The domed cathedral on Toompea, free and open 08:00 to 18:00 every day; 4.6 on Google from 8,935 reviews, so it is on every tour, and 30 minutes at opening is the way to do it.

places.name: Kohtuotsa viewing platform
places.note: The main Toompea platform over the old town roofs, free and open at all hours, 4.8 on Google from 6,923 reviews; busier than Patkuli a few minutes away, so come early or after dark.

places.name: Saaremaa Veski
places.note: Dinner inside an old windmill, White Guide 2026; the pork belly is EUR 17 and the cheese balls EUR 8 (menu checked November 2026). Open Wednesday to Saturday only, Sunday to Tuesday is for groups of 20 or more.

places.name: Resto HAFEN
places.note: Harbour restaurant for the fish soup, the daily fish pasta or bao. The price is a $20 to $30 range (EnPrimeur, October 2026), so $25 is the midpoint; from September to May Monday is lunch only, 12:00 to 15:00.

places.name: Castello
places.note: Italian-style place on the castle street, Falstaff Recommended, for pizza on a simple night. The price is a $20 to $30 range (EnPrimeur, October 2026), so $25 is the midpoint; later than 21:00 except on Sundays.

places.name: Kaali Crater
places.note: The meteorite crater at Kaali, free and open air with no gate, 4.6 on Google from 612 reviews; 45 minutes, and the small meteoritics museum is next to it.

places.name: Kaali meteoritics and limestone museum
places.note: Small museum beside the crater, about $2 and listed 10:00 to 18:00 every day; winter hours are unverified, so check, and 30 minutes covers it.

places.name: Karja church
places.note: Village church in Karja in the north of the island, 4.6 on Google from 218 reviews; the only fixed time found is the Sunday 11:00 service, so hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Sõrve Lighthouse
places.note: The lighthouse at the tip of the Sõrve peninsula, 4.8 on Google from 4,619 reviews and about $8 to go up; it opens to the public in summer only, so it is closed now.

places.name: Muhu Museum (Koguva)
places.note: The Muhu Museum in Koguva village, about $8 (price since January 2025), listed 10:00 to 17:00 every day; winter hours are unverified, so check, and pair it with the Eemu windmill on Muhu.

places.name: Suur Tõll and Piret sculpture
places.note: The Suur Tõll and Piret sculpture in Kuressaare, free and open at all hours; 15 minutes on the walk between the castle and the harbour.

places.name: Muhu St Catherine's Church
places.note: St Catherine's on Muhu, 4.5 on Google from 325 reviews; it is listed 10:00 to 16:00 with no daily schedule, so hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Eemu windmill
places.note: The Eemu windmill on Muhu, EUR 1 to go in, 10:00 to 18:00 Wednesday to Sunday, closed Mondays and Tuesdays; winter hours are unverified, so check, and 30 minutes is plenty.

places.name: Angla Windmill Hill
places.note: The windmill hill at Angla, 4.5 on Google from 1,427 reviews, open 10:00 to 18:00 every day from September to April; no price found, so check the price, and combine it with Karja church nearby.

places.name: Kaarma church
places.note: Kaarma's church, about 11 km north of Kuressaare and 4.7 on Google; it opens daily only from 1 June to 31 August, so it is closed for winter now, and check the price.

places.name: Laurentiuse church
places.note: St Lawrence's church in the middle of Kuressaare, a few minutes' walk from Saaremaa Veski; no hours found, so hours vary, check, and check the price.

outings.why: The Viru bog boardwalk is short and easy, Palmse Manor gives you the baltic-German estate history, but it's a long day for a fairly light walk.
outings.name: Lahemaa: Viru bog boardwalk and Palmse Manor
outings.season: year-round, boardwalk can ice up in winter

destination.name: Estonia
destination.pitch: Medieval Tallinn plus Saaremaa's cliffs and bog give you a week that's varied without needing Riga or Helsinki bolted on.
destination.caveat: You will land tired off a connection through Helsinki, Frankfurt, or Riga since there's no direct flight from the US. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Tallinn's compact walkable core rewards a few days without a car.
because.nature: Saaremaa gives you cliffs, a bog boardwalk, and open countryside.
because.culture: Tallinn's old town is one of the best-preserved medieval cores in Europe.
because.exploration: Lahemaa's bog trails and Saaremaa's back roads get you off the old town cobbles.
